([[Bel Aire, Kansas]]) | college = * [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]] (2018–2020) * [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]] (2022–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | career_start = 2024 | career_end = | years1 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team1 = [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team2 = [[Rip City Remix]] | years3 = {{nbay|2025|end}}–present | team3 = [[Utah Jazz]] | years4 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team4 = →[[Salt Lake City Stars]] | highlights = * NBA G League Next Up Game (2026) * First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2024) * Second-team All-ACC (2023) }} '''Blake Demond Hinson''' (born December 26, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Utah Jazz]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss Rebels]] and the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Hinson grew up in [[Deltona, Florida]] and initially attended [[Deltona High School]]. He transferred to [[Sunrise Christian Academy]] in [[Bel Aire, Kansas]] before the start of his senior season.{{cite web|title=Two-sport star Blake Hinson departs Deltona for Kansas' Sunrise Christian Academy|url=https://www.news-journalonline.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2017/08/05/two-sport-star-blake-hinson-departs-deltona-for-kansas-sunrise-christian-academy/20012859007/|work=[[The Daytona Beach News-Journal]]|date=August 5, 2017|access-date=March 12, 2024}} ==College career== Hinson began his college career at [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]]. He started 31 games and averaged 8.3 points and 2.9 rebounds as a freshman.{{cite web|title=How Blake Hinson grew from 'extreme, stupid confidence' to become a record holder at Pitt|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2024/03/09/blake-hinson-final-month-acc-college-basketball-profile-ncaa-tournament/stories/202403050078|work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|date=March 9, 2024|access-date=March 12, 2024}} Hinson averaged 10.1 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 1.4 assists during his sophomore season.{{cite web|title=Iowa State basketball: Blake Hinson healthy after sitting out season|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/cyclone-insider/2021/07/02/iowa-state-cyclones-basketball-blake-hinson-healthy-2021-2022-season/7837014002/|work=[[The Des Moines Register]]|date=July 2, 2017|access-date=March 12, 2024}} After the season, he entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|title=Report: Deltona native, Ole Miss junior Blake Hinson enters transfer portal|url=https://www.news-journalonline.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2020/06/17/report-deltona-native-ole-miss-junior-blake-hinson-enters-transfer-portal/42111395/|work=[[The Daytona Beach News-Journal]]|date=June 17, 2020|access-date=March 12, 2024}} Hinson transferred to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]].{{cite web|title=Iowa State men's basketball: Cyclones land Mississippi transfer Blake Hinson|url=https://www.amestrib.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2020/06/24/iowa-state-men8217s-basketball-cyclones-land-mississippi-transfer-blake-hinson/42110261/|work=[[Ames Tribune]]|date=June 24, 2024|access-date=March 12, 2024}} He missed his first season with the Cyclones due to an unspecified medical condition.{{cite web|first=Dave|last=Wilson|title=Iowa State's Blake Hinson to miss basketball season with medical condition|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29915821/iowa-state-blake-hinson-miss-season-medical-condition|work=[[ESPN.com]]|date=September 18, 2020|access-date=March 12, 2024}} Hinson left the program shortly before the start of the 2021–2022 season.{{cite web|title=Blake Hinson is leaving the Iowa State men's basketball program|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/cyclone-insider/2021/10/23/blake-hinson-leaving-iowa-state-mens-basketball-program-roster/6155541001/|work=[[The Des Moines Register]]|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=March 12, 2024}} Hinson transferred a second time to [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]].{{cite web|title=Pitt lands commitment from Iowa State transfer Blake Hinson|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2022/04/18/pitt-basketball-commits-2022-blake-hinson-iowa-state-transfer-jeff-capel-panthers/stories/202204180093|work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|date=April 18, 2022|access-date=March 12, 2024}} He was named second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) in his first season with the team after averaging 15.3 points and 6.0 rebounds.{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Eisenberg|title='Heckling is what I live for': Pitt's Blake Hinson explains 'disrespectful' celebration at Duke|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/heckling-is-what-i-live-for-pitts-blake-hinson-explains-disrespectful-celebration-at-duke-141905231.html|work=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=January 23, 2024|access-date=March 12, 2024}} Hinson was named first-team All-ACC in his final season at Pitt.{{cite web|title=Pitt's Blake Hinson, Bub Carrington, Ishmael Leggett earn All-ACC honors|url=https://triblive.com/sports/pitts-blake-hinson-bub-carrington-ishmael-leggett-earn-all-acc-honors/|work=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]]|date=March 11, 2024|access-date=March 12, 2024}} He averaged 18.5 points per game and set a school record with 110 made three-pointers.{{cite web|title=Panthers Decline Invitation to NIT|url=https://pittsburghpanthers.com/news/2024/3/17/mens-basketball-panthers-decline-invitation-to-nit.aspx|work=[[Pittsburgh Panthers]]|date=March 17, 2024|access-date=March 18, 2024}} ==Professional career== After going unselected in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Hinson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on July 5, 2024,{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Blake Hinson and Armel Traore to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-sign-blake-hinson-and-armel-traore-to-two-way-contracts-070524|website=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2024|access-date=July 5, 2024}} but was waived on September 16{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Christian Koloko to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-sign-christian-koloko-to-two-way-contract-091624|website=NBA.com|date=September 16, 2024|access-date=September 16, 2024}}{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Stinar|title=Los Angeles Lakers Reportedly Release Talented 3-Point Shooter|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/los-angeles-lakers-reportedly-release-talented-3-point-shooter-hinson|website=SI.com|date=September 16, 2024|access-date=September 17, 2024}} and seven days later, he signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Warriors Sign Blake Hinson To Exhibit 10 Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/warriors-to-sign-blake-hinson-to-exhibit-10-contract.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 24, 2024|access-date=September 25, 2024}} However, he was waived on October 19{{cite web|title=Warriors Waive Blake Hinson, Kevin Knox II & Jackson Rowe|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/blake-hinson-kevin-knox-ii-jackson-rowe-waived-20241019|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 22, 2024}} and nine days later, he joined the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]].{{cite web|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Announce 2024 Training Camp Roster|url=https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2024-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 1, 2024}} On March 28, 2025, Hinson tied a Santa Cruz record with 10 made three-pointers, as he scored a career-high 44 points in a 150-105 rout of the [[Rip City Remix]].{{Cite web|title=Blake Hinson scores 44 as Warriors blast Rip City, qualify for playoffs|url=https://www.santacruzsentinel.com/2025/03/29/blake-hinson-scores-44-as-warriors-blast-rip-city-qualify-for-playoffs-nba-g-league/|access-date=May 30, 2025|website=santacruzsentinel.com|language=en}} For the [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–26 season]], Hinson was added to the roster of the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Rip City Remix]]. On February 9, 2026, Hinson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|title= Utah Jazz Sign Blake Hinson to Two-Way Contract |url= https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-blake-hinson-to-two-way-contract |website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2026|access-date=February 12, 2026}} On February 28, Hinson made his first career NBA start in a home game against the New Orleans Pelicans.{{cite web |last1=Rotowire Staff |title=Blake Hinson News: Drawing first NBA start |url=https://www.rotowire.com/basketball/headlines/blake-hinson-news-drawing-first-nba-start-521002 |website=Rotowire |access-date=February 28, 2026 |date=February 28, 2026}} He was moved into the starting lineup in place of [[John Konchar]].{{cite web |title=New Orleans Pelicans vs. Utah Jazz - February 28, 2026 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/nop-vs-uta-0022500858/box-score |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 28, 2026 |date=February 28, 2026}} On April 11, Hinson scored a career-high 30 points in a 147–101 win over the [[2025–26 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/utah-jazz/jazz-news-the-insane-triple-double-history-made-in-tank-off-vs-grizzlies|title=The insane triple-double history made in egregious tank-off Jazz vs. Grizzlies|website=ClutchPoints|last=Ojeda|first=Julian|date=April 11, 2026|access-date=April 11, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401811036|title=Hinson scores a career-high
